title: Faster and more rotational Anthrobots cover more of a neuronal scratch

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Faster and more rotational Anthrobots cover more of a neuronal scratch

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Anthrobots can move across scratches in human neuronal monolayers in vitro, and bots with higher rotational tendency or higher speed cover a larger proportion of unique positions along the scratch interface.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Results › Anthrobots Can Move Across Scratches on Live Monolayers In Vitro

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Taken together, these data reveal that Anthrobots are capable of efficiently moving across damaged tissues, and that bots that have a higher rotational tendency and or higher speed have higher degrees of unique coordinate coverage by moving across a higher percentage of the scratch interface.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Gumuskaya G, Srivastava P, Cooper BG, Lesser H, Semegran B, Garnier S, Levin M, “Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells”, Advanced science (Weinheim, Baden-Wurttemberg, Germany) (2024), doi:10.1002/advs.202303575; section “Results › Anthrobots Can Move Across Scratches on Live Monolayers In Vitro”. Scope: NHBE-derived Anthrobots in scratched monolayers of hiNSC-derived human neurons, n = 17 bots

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2024-anthrobots-18: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.71

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: All key variables and statistical criteria are explicit, and public media allow a partial reanalysis. The small filtered sample does not adequately support a broad efficiency relationship.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Re-track the 17 usable bots and regress unique scratch-interface coverage on rotational tendency and instantaneous speed with scratch geometry and contact time as covariates.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Only 17 selected trajectories were analyzed.

Scratch shape, contact opportunity, and bot size may confound both predictors.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.97
analysis feasibility: 0.88
data adequacy: 0.38
discriminating power: 0.7
data existence: 0.66

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Coverage, rotation and speed are defined indices, and the paper gives slopes and sample size for the scratch trials. Those tracks are not public. The correlations are checkable in principle and confounded in practice, and neither the fit nor the confounds can be re-estimated from the published summary.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For bots on scratched neuronal monolayers, regress the fraction of unique positions visited along the scratch on rotational tendency and on speed. Positive slopes would support greater coverage by faster or more rotational bots; flat or negative slopes would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Speed and rotation can proxy bot size or tracking quality rather than coverage strategy.

Bots that never touched the scratch were excluded, so the sample is conditioned on interaction.

The 17 tracked scratch trials are not deposited.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.2
discriminating power: 0.48
data adequacy: 0.16
data existence: 0.18
operationalizability: 0.88
